aspects.says: lockInterruptibly() and tryLock go before the try, so that a failed attempt never runs unlock(): inside it, IllegalMonitorStateException replaces InterruptedException, or an outer hold is silently lost.
basis: section:lock() Waits Until It Gets the Lock; tryLock and lockInterruptibly Can Give Up

aspects.says: A woken thread can find the state changed by another thread, or wake spuriously, so await() is called in a while loop over its condition.
basis: section:Spot the Problem: if Around await()

aspects.says: await() releases every hold of the waiting thread and restores them before it returns.
basis: section:A Condition Gives Up the Lock While It Waits, So Check Again After await()

aspects.says: A non-fair lock lets newcomers barge ahead of waiting threads, which gives it several times the throughput of a fair lock; a fair lock serves the longest waiter.
basis: section:A Non-Fair Lock Lets a Newcomer Go First; a Fair Lock Queues, and Costs Throughput
aspects.reason: throughput and barging counts depend on scheduling and load; a deterministic test can't show them, and the page shows measured runs

aspects.says: lock() keeps waiting through an interrupt, while lockInterruptibly() answers it with InterruptedException and doesn't take the lock.
basis: section:lock() Waits Until It Gets the Lock; tryLock and lockInterruptibly Can Give Up

aspects.says: A thread holding the read lock that asks for the write lock waits for itself forever, and new readers and writers queue behind it; release the read lock first, and downgrading is allowed.
basis: section:Spot the Problem: Loading on a Miss

aspects.says: Only the thread that holds a ReentrantLock can unlock it; unlock() from another thread throws IllegalMonitorStateException.
basis: section:The Lock Counts Holds: One unlock() per lock(), by the Thread That Holds It

aspects.says: Any number of threads can hold a read lock together, while the write lock excludes readers and writers.
basis: section:A Read-Write Lock Lets Readers Share, but a Reader Can't Upgrade

aspects.says: After trading the read lock for the write lock, the cache looks again before loading, since another thread may have loaded the entry in the gap.
basis: section:Spot the Problem: Loading on a Miss
aspects.reason: the double load needs two misses in the gap between releasing the read lock and taking the write lock, which no test can force through this API without a hook in the reader's code

aspects.says: The lock counts holds per thread: the owner relocks at once, and the lock is free only after one unlock() per lock(), so a path that locks twice and unlocks once keeps it held.
basis: section:The Lock Counts Holds: One unlock() per lock(), by the Thread That Holds It
section:Spot the Problem: One Path Locks Twice

aspects.says: Each change signals the condition the side that can now proceed waits on; signalling the wrong one leaves the waiter parked, and one shared condition needs signalAll().
basis: section:Signal the Condition Its Waiters Wait On

aspects.says: A timed tryLock gives a caller a budget and returns whether it got the lock; code that ignores the result runs unguarded and then fails in unlock().
basis: section:lock() Waits Until It Gets the Lock; tryLock and lockInterruptibly Can Give Up

aspects.says: The untimed tryLock() takes a free lock even on a fair lock with threads queued; tryLock(0, SECONDS) respects the queue.
basis: section:A Non-Fair Lock Lets a Newcomer Go First; a Fair Lock Queues, and Costs Throughput

aspects.says: Nothing releases a ReentrantLock but unlock(): an exception, the end of a task or of the thread leaves it held, so the unlock goes in a finally after a lock() taken before the try.
basis: section:Nothing Releases a ReentrantLock but unlock(), So Unlock in finally
